title: Every Full Tree With N Nodes
statement:
A binary tree is full when every node has either zero or two children, never exactly one.

Given n, build every distinct full binary tree with exactly n nodes. Every node holds the value 0; only the shapes differ. Return the list of their roots. Any order of the trees is accepted.

Different trees in your answer may share subtree nodes. Each tree is compared by its level-order listing.

examples.why: The root's two children are a leaf and a 3-node tree. The 3-node tree can hang on the left or on the right.
A root with two leaves is the only option.
A full tree adds nodes two at a time, so it always has an odd node count.

hints: Remove the root. What is left on each side must itself be a full tree.
If the left subtree has i nodes, the right has n − 1 − i. Both must be odd. Combine every left shape with every right shape.
The same sizes come up again and again. Cache the list of trees for each size.

explain.intuition:
A full tree with more than one node is a root plus a full left subtree plus a full right subtree. So pick how many nodes go left, i, leaving n − 1 − i on the right. For every pair (a left shape of size i, a right shape of that size) you get one new tree. Since full trees always have an odd count, only odd i matter, and an even n has no answer at all.

Many recursive calls ask for the same size, so store the list for each size and reuse it. The trees then share subtree objects, which is fine: nobody mutates them, much like immutable state in a frontend store that shares unchanged branches.
steps: If n is even, return an empty list. If n = 1, return a single leaf.
For each odd i from 1 to n − 2: get all trees of size i and of size n − 1 − i.
For every left tree and every right tree, create a new root with those children and add it to the result.
Cache the result for n before returning it.
pitfalls: Looping over even left sizes too. They return empty lists, which hides the bug, but wastes time.
Creating one root object outside the inner loop and reassigning its children. All entries then point to the same node and show the last shape.

complexity.time: O(Cₖ · n) where k = (n − 1) / 2 and Cₖ is the Catalan number

solutions.title: Plain recursion
solutions.idea: Split the remaining n − 1 nodes between the two sides in every odd way and combine every pair of shapes. No caching.

solutions.title: Recursion with a cache per size
solutions.idea: Build the list for each size once. Larger trees reuse the cached smaller trees as their subtrees.

followups: Return only the count of full trees with n nodes. Can you do it without building them?
Callers want to mutate the trees they receive. What must change, and what does it cost?
